title: Adjustment of Duty Rates via SROs
summary: This thread tracks the frequent, targeted adjustments of duty rates for specific H.S. Codes and industrial categories through SROs. Over time, the mechanism shifted from simple rate modifications to complex table-based structures involving Margin of Preference (MoP) and alignment with the Customs Act, 2023.

evolution.legal_basis: Shifted from Customs Act, 1969 to Customs Act, 2023.
evolution.structure: Evolved from simple percentage changes to complex multi-column tables with MoP and conditional exemptions.
evolution.scope: Expanded from general goods to specific industrial categories and VAT-compliant manufacturers.

timeline.change: Direct reduction of duty percentage for specific goods.
Introduction of conditional duty rates based on H.S. Code and statutory rate thresholds.
Implementation of specific duty tables for industrial raw materials.
Integration of Regulatory Duty and Supplementary Duty adjustments alongside Customs Duty.
Formalization of Margin of Preference (MoP) calculations and clarification of exclusive applicability.
Transition to the legal framework of the Customs Act, 2023 for industrial raw material duty concessions.

Customs Act 1969: Section 19(1) of this Act empowers the government to grant exemptions and make amendments to existing customs notifications.
Value Added Tax Act 1991: Section 14(1) of this Act provides the legal authority for the government, in consultation with the National Board of Revenue, to amend fiscal notifications in the public interest.
National Board of Revenue: The government is required to consult with the National Board of Revenue before exercising its powers to amend customs and tax notifications.
S.R.O. 157-AIN/2012: This existing customs notification is amended to adjust specific duty rates, clarify exclusions for machine parts, and update HS Code entries within the referenced table.
Bangladesh Customs Tariff: The table of HS Codes within the tariff structure is updated by adding new codes, replacing existing ones, and deleting obsolete entries to maintain accurate classification of goods.

Customs Act 1969: Section 18(2) of this Act empowers the Government to impose Regulatory Duty on goods imported into Bangladesh.
The Act governs the framework for the First Schedule, which contains the H.S. Code classifications and duty rates.
Regulatory Duty: This SRO imposes a 3% Regulatory Duty on a wide range of goods generally, while specifying distinct rates for items listed in TABLE-II.
The duty applies in addition to existing tax structures, subject to specific exemptions for items listed in the provided exclusions and those covered by previous SROs and government orders.
TABLE-I: This table lists specific goods and their corresponding H.S. Codes that are exempted from the general 3% Regulatory Duty imposed by this order.
TABLE-II: This table lists specific goods, H.S. Codes, and their respective Regulatory Duty rates, ranging from 3% to 20%, which differ from the general 3% rate established for other items.
Import Duty: The order references the statutory rate of import duty to delineate the scope of goods subject to the new Regulatory Duty.
H.S. Code: H.S. Codes are utilized to precisely identify the categories of goods subject to or exempted from the Regulatory Duty imposed by this order.

(১) সংশ্লিষ্ট আমদানিকারককে Industrial IRC holder VAT compliant উৎপাদনকারী শিল্প (Manufacturing industry) হইতে হইবে;
ব্যাখ্যা:

(আ) VAT compliant অর্থ মূল্য সংযোজন কর ও সম্পূরক শুল্ক আইন, ২০১২ ও মূল্য সংযোজন কর ও সম্পূরক শুল্ক বিধিমালা, ২০১৬ এর অধীন নিবন্ধিত নিয়মিত দাখিলপত্র (রিটার্ন) দাখিল করে এইরূপ উৎপাদনকারী প্রতিষ্ঠান;
(২) এই প্রজ্ঞাপনের আওতায় পণ্য আমদানি ও খালাসের লক্ষ্যে প্রতিষ্ঠানটির হালনাগাদ নবায়নকৃত শিল্প ভোক্তা আইআরসি রহিয়াছে এবং ১৩ ডিজিট সংবলিত মূল্য সংযোজন কর (মূসক) নিবন্ধিত প্রতিষ্ঠানটি বিবেচ্য বিল অব এন্ট্রি দাখিলের অব্যবহিত পূর্ববর্তী মাসের মূসক দাখিলপত্র (রিটার্ন) দাখিল করিয়াছে মর্মে কাস্টমস কম্পিউটার সিস্টেমে বা ভ্যাট অনলাইন সিস্টেমে বা জাতীয় রাজস্ব বোর্ড এর ওয়েবসাইটে বা ভ্যাট কমিশনারেট এর ওয়েবসাইটে ইলেকট্রনিক তথ্য প্রদর্শিত থাকিতে হইবে:
তবে শর্ত থাকে যে, কোনো দৈব-দুর্বিপাক বা কোনো যৌক্তিক কারণে ইলেকট্রনিক তথ্য পাওয়া সম্ভব না হইলে সংশ্লিষ্ট কমিশনার অব কাস্টমস প্রতি ক্ষেত্রে কারণ লিপিবদ্ধ করিয়া শুল্কায়নের প্রয়োজনীয় কার্যক্রম গ্রহণ করিতে পারিবে।

Customs Act 2023: This SRO is issued under the authority granted by Section 25(1) of the Customs Act 2023.
The Act provides the legal basis for granting exemptions on customs duties and regulatory duties for specific industrial raw materials.
Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty A: This SRO is issued under the authority granted by Section 126(1) of the Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty Act 2012.
The Act defines the VAT compliance requirements that industries must meet to qualify for duty exemptions.
National Board of Revenue: The Board is the regulatory body consulted for the issuance of this SRO and the establishment of its duty exemption framework.
Industrial IRC Holder: An Industrial IRC holder is defined as an entity possessing a valid Industrial Consumer IRC issued by the Office of the Chief Controller of Imports and Exports.
Only manufacturers holding this status are eligible for the specific customs duty, supplementary duty, and regulatory duty exemptions listed in the order.
VAT Compliant: An entity is considered VAT compliant if it is registered under the Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty Act 2012 and the associated Rules, and regularly submits its VAT returns.
Compliance status must be verifiable through the customs or VAT online systems to benefit from the tax exemptions provided in this order.
H.S. Code: The SRO specifies various H.S. Codes in its six tables, identifying the raw materials eligible for duty concessions when imported by qualifying industries.
The applicable duty rates for imports are determined based on the specific H.S. Code and the corresponding industrial category.

Customs Duty: The SRO grants exemptions or reductions on the customs duties specified in the First Schedule of the Customs Act for defined raw materials used by industrial manufacturers.
Supplementary Duty: The order provides exemptions for supplementary duties that exceed the rates specified in the relevant columns of the tables for eligible industrial imports.
